purpose: Compare multiple numeric series over the same ordered x-axis.

rawDataContract.notes: Rows may be wide or tidy. Convert tidy rows to the payload style expected by the script if needed.

semanticChannels.semantics: multiple comparable numeric measures or entities
reader-facing y-axis description or metric name, such as 累计收益率; ordinary grouped-line charts should use the right y-axis only

payloadShape.title: string
payloadShape.xScale: category (default) | time (ISO dates / epoch ms) | linear (numbers)

modelInstructions: In Mentora use the existing source JSON file via payload.dataSource.path/recordsPath/fields instead of copying rows or writing a conversion script for simple field/date mappings. Read hostExtensions.dataSource for the exact contract; run this concrete script through skill_runner.py execute.
visualStyle.chart.fitContent=true sizes an embedded chart frame from actual root, SVG text/legend and tooltip bounds without the default footer-height reserve; content must stay fully visible.

pointMarkers.allowCurveOverlap defaults false. When true, prefer vertical gaps and minimize covered curve length; allow limited overlap only when needed, while protecting marked anchors, card spacing and plot bounds; keep normal card typography/padding.
Use no more than 6-8 visible series unless the user explicitly asks.
For ordinary grouped-line examples, bind every series to axis='right', set leftAxis.visible=false, set rightAxis.visible=true, and set visualStyle.yAxis.position='right'.

For event-window cumulative-return charts with xField day/window_day/relative_day, provide one row for every integer day in the window and forward-fill weekends/holidays. If early non-trading days are missing, use 0 until the first trading-day return appears.
The renderer defaults visualStyle.line.connectNulls=true as a safety net, but source payloads should still repair breakpoints in data rather than relying only on rendering.
Put the metric name in rightAxis.label. Do not set series[].suffix, leftAxis.suffix, or rightAxis.suffix unless the user explicitly asks for units on visible values.
Do not set leftAxis.min/max or rightAxis.min/max unless the user explicitly requests fixed axis bounds. Let the renderer derive a readable domain from the actual data.
If units are semantically important, mention them in surrounding prose or the axis label text only when requested; do not append units to y-axis tick labels or legend/tooltip values by default.
Use a second axis only when the user explicitly asks for dual-axis comparison or the series have incompatible scales.
Tooltip positioning must clamp to both viewport edges; at the first x point, keep the tooltip fully visible instead of allowing its left side to be clipped.
The tooltip arrow should visually attach to the tooltip body with a slight overlap, and its tip must align with the vertical position line even when the tooltip is clamped at the viewport edge.
On small screens, compute tooltip anchor coordinates from the rendered SVG screen position, not only from unscaled SVG/viewBox coordinates.
When the tooltip is clamped at the left or right viewport boundary and the arrow tip would sit on the tooltip edge, hide the arrow instead of showing a clipped or detached triangle.

For right-side y-axes, align the y-axis description to the same right edge as the y-axis tick labels, and allow the description text to extend leftward into the chart area instead of reserving extra right margin.

For a framed two-line event annotation, use visualStyle.overlays[] with type='pointMarkers', x or index, labelBox=true, eventTime for the first line, and eventTitle for the second line. Preserve all base grouped-line defaults unless the user explicitly requests a visual override.

For a verified trade/event date color boundary, use visualStyle.line.colorSplit with an exact x present in data. Bind event points with existing pointMarkers; never shift missing dates. Keep all base layout and line defaults.

When mark cards must not cover curves, set pointMarkers.labelPlacement=outside-top. The renderer reserves a separate label lane above the SVG plot, wraps all labels on narrow widths and connects exact price points; original plot coordinates and styling remain unchanged.

For irregular observation dates use xScale=time and sorted ISO dates or epoch milliseconds. Step-after holds the previous value until the next observation; step-before changes at the previous observation. missingValuePolicy=gap preserves missing observations and disconnects the line; never fill nulls silently.

visualStyle.line: Existing line defaults plus optional colorSplit: {x:exact existing x,field:series field,beforeColor,afterColor,beforeLabel,afterLabel}. Changes stroke colors and legend only; same coordinates/path. Missing x leaves ordinary line unchanged.; curve: straight|smooth|step-after|step-before

dataSource.purpose: Pass a verified local JSON file directly; the host maps fields and checks rendered values without model transcription.
dataSource.payload: Keep normal renderer fields (xField, series/yField, axes, visualStyle). Omit data/rows when dataSource is used. No scaling or filling is performed.
dataSource.pieMapping: For pie.py map source fields to label/value; nonnegative finite values and positive total required. Missing values must be handled explicitly upstream, never silently zero-filled.
dataSource.lineOptions: xScale=time for irregular ISO dates/epoch ms; visualStyle.line.curve=step-after|step-before|straight|smooth; missingValuePolicy=gap preserves nulls.
dataSource.receipt: chartValidation reports source hash, rows, per-series valid/missing counts, min/max, first/last observations and axis coverage. Verified chart HTML can be passed to StreamViz chart_artifacts without copying data or drawing SVG coordinates.

hostExtensions.standalone: Direct component CLI still receives ordinary data; host expands dataSource before execution.
